# DSP Architecture: TENSION

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during Stages 1-4 implementation. It grounds the authoritative `implementation-spec.md` (which wins on any conflict) in JUCE 8 APIs and resolves the spec's open questions. It does NOT redesign the spec's 10 named modules.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (research-planning-agent), 2026-10-29
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Foundation/Shell), Stage 3 (DSP phases), Stage 4 (GUI phases)
**Complexity tier:** 6 (DEEP) - coordinated 10-module engine, host-tempo sync, feedback paths, real-time reactive visualizer
**Plugin type:** Audio effect (mono/stereo in, same out). `IS_SYNTH FALSE`. Generates sound from silence via internal noise, but still an effect (has an input bus; no MIDI).

| # | Feature | Kind |
|---|---------|------|
| 1 | TensionEngine (controller / per-block orchestration) | DSP |
| 2 | TensionMapping (nonlinear curves + 3 rise modes + mode crossfade) | DSP/control |
| 3 | LFOEngine (5 shapes, free / host-BPM sync, 4 destinations) | DSP |
| 4 | NoiseGenerator (white/pink/filtered, deterministic, riser curve) | DSP |

Each is documented below. Features 3-10 are the spec's module list verbatim.

## Core Components

### TensionEngine
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (orchestrator). Owns all modules below; no JUCE base class.
- **Purpose:** Per-block controller. Reads smoothed parameters, evaluates `TensionMapping` once per control-rate sub-block, pushes the resulting destination targets into each module, runs the audio chain, and publishes visualizer telemetry.
- **Parameters Affected:** tension, mix, output, sync, riseMode (all)
- **Module:** `juce_audio_processors`, `juce_dsp`
- **Configuration:**
  - Internally ALWAYS 2 channels (mono input is duplicated to L/R on entry, averaged back on exit if the host layout is mono).
  - **Control rate:** audio is processed in sub-blocks of at most 32 samples; mapping + smoother stepping + filter-coefficient/delay-time/reverb-parameter updates happen once per sub-block. Block-size invariance is a test requirement (output must not depend on host block size beyond float rounding).
  - `prepare(sampleRate, maxBlock, numChannels)` preallocates ALL buffers (scratch, delay lines at max 2.5 s x 2 ch, predelay, noise scratch). `processBlock` is allocation-free.
  - Transparent fast path: if smoothed engagement `e == 0`, tension target `== 0`, and tail energy trackers < -120 dBFS, skip the whole wet chain and copy input to output (see Zero-Tension Transparency).
  - Lifecycle: `prepare`, `reset`, `process(AudioBuffer<float>&, const HostTransport&)`, `getTelemetry()` (lock-free).

### TensionMapping
- **JUCE Class:** Custom, pure functions (no JUCE dependency except `juce::jlimit`/`juce::jmap` helpers). Header-only candidates; fully unit-testable without audio.
- **Purpose:** Converts `(tension t in [0,1], RiseMode)` into a flat `TensionTargets` struct of ~30 destination values. Each destination has its OWN independent curve (smoothstep / exponential / power / musical-octave) - nothing is linear in t.
- **Parameters Affected:** tension, riseMode
- **Configuration:**
  - Curve primitives: `smooth(a,b,t)` = smoothstep; `expo(t,k) = (e^{kt}-1)/(e^k-1)`; `pw(t,p)`; `oct(f0, octaves, c)` = `f0 * 2^(octaves*c)` for frequencies (musical = equal perceptual steps); `dB(lo,hi,c)` = dB-linear interpolation then `dbToGain` (ported idea from DROP noise curves).
  - Three profiles are parameter sets, not different code: each destination curve takes `(start, end, exponent)` per mode.
  - **Mode switching:** the engine evaluates the OLD and NEW profile and linearly crossfades the resulting `TensionTargets` struct with a 600 ms smoothed `modeBlend` (0..1), so changing riseMode mid-automation never jumps.
  - See "Master Tension Map" under Algorithm Details for the full destination table.

### LFOEngine
- **JUCE Class:** Custom oscillator (phase accumulator). Uses `juce::dsp::LookupTableTransform` NOT needed - sine via `std::sin` at control+audio rate is cheap enough; may use `juce::dsp::FastMathApproximations::sin` if profiling demands. Random for S&H from deterministic xorshift32.
- **Purpose:** Provide modulation sources for amplitude (tremolo), filter cutoff, stereo movement, delay-time wobble. Shapes: sine, triangle, saw, reverse saw, sample-and-hold.
- **Parameters Affected:** tension (rate, depth), sync, riseMode (shape per destination)
- **Configuration:**
  - Two instances: `lfoA` (amplitude + filter), `lfoB` (stereo + delay, rate ratio 0.75 of A, phase offset 90 degrees) so destinations do not move in lock-step.
  - **Free mode:** rate in Hz from the mapping (0.15 Hz -> ~9 Hz, exponential in t).
  - **Sync mode:** `rateHz = (bpm/60) * cyclesPerBeat`, with `cyclesPerBeat` from the mapping (1/8 -> 4 cycles/beat across the knob), soft-snapped toward the power-of-two ladder (1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1, 2, 4 per beat) using a smoothstep "dwell" in log2 domain (snap strength 0.6) so the rise accelerates through musical grids while staying continuous. Fallback if the snap is not convincing: pure continuous tempo-scaled rate.
  - **Phase continuity:** phase is integrated (`phase += rate/fs`) so rate changes from the knob never cause phase jumps. On transport start (host `isPlaying` false -> true) in sync mode, phase is re-aligned once to `frac(ppq * cyclesPerBeat)`. No per-sample ppq locking (would jump on rate change).
  - Tempo fallback 120 BPM when the host provides none (Standalone).
  - S&H: new random value at each cycle wrap, 2 ms one-pole slew to prevent clicks. Seedable (`setSeed`).
  - Output bipolar [-1,1]; consumers scale by their own depth curve.
  - Rate is slewed in the log domain (120 ms) - "accelerating" feel without Doppler-like warble.

### NoiseGenerator
- **JUCE Class:** Custom RNG + `juce::dsp::StateVariableTPTFilter<float>` (HP / BP / LP) ; `juce::SmoothedValue` for gain.
- **Purpose:** Independent parallel signal generator. Noise rises in level and brightness with tension; silent at tension 0 so the plugin generates risers from silence.
- **Parameters Affected:** tension, riseMode, sync (LFO tremolo on noise), mix (noise is part of the wet bus)
- **Configuration:**
  - **Deterministic RNG:** xorshift32 per channel (never `juce::Random` global, never `std::rand`), seeds `seedL = S`, `seedR = S ^ 0x9E3779B9`. `setSeed()` + `reset()` restore bit-identical output. RNG advances every sample even when the gain is 0, so output is independent of automation history (DROP lesson).
  - **Colors:** white (uniform [-1,1]); pink (Paul Kellett 3-pole-per-octave cascaded one-pole filter, normalised); "filtered" = white through a resonant band-pass whose center rises with tension (the rising sweep). The engine blends `pink -> white` by a brightness curve so the spectral tilt brightens as tension rises, then a rising HPF (clears low mud) and a closing/opening LPF shape the top.
  - **Level curve:** dB-linear: `noiseDb = lerp(-66, ceil_dB(mode), expo-ish curve)` gated by `smooth(0.04, 0.28, t)` so gain is EXACTLY 0 at t=0 and "begins emerging" near 25%. `ceil_dB` per mode: Slow Burn -20, Cinematic -16, Aggressive -12 (dBFS RMS-ish).
  - Own modulation: tremolo from `lfoA` (depth rises with t) and cutoff sweep; decorrelated L/R streams give natural width, additionally scaled by the width curve.
  - Own gain smoothing (40 ms); brightness/cutoff smoothing (60 ms).

### FilterEngine
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::StateVariableTPTFilter<float>` (`juce_dsp`) - LowPass / HighPass / BandPass, stable under per-sample cutoff changes (TPT topology), `setResonance` maps to Q.
- **Purpose:** Pre-Filter stage (spectral thinning + resonant sweep) with smooth, modulated cutoff.
- **Parameters Affected:** tension, riseMode, lfoA (cutoff modulation)
- **Configuration:**
  - Two stages in the series path: **HP** (cutoff rises 20 Hz -> ~650 Hz Cinematic, expo; classic riser "thinning") and a **resonant band-pass sweep** blended in parallel (blend 0 -> 0.30, center 300 Hz -> 9 kHz, `oct()` mapping; resonance Q 0.9 -> 3.2).
  - Resonance is hard-capped (`Q <= 4.0`) and cutoff clamped to `[20 Hz, 0.45 fs]` -> unconditional stability (TPT SVF is stable for all Q > 0). Resonance rise is scaled down as the BP center rises above 6 kHz to avoid harshness (spec priority: "avoid harsh resonance").
  - Cutoff modulated by lfoA in octaves (`cutoff *= 2^(depth*lfo)`), depth rises with t (0 -> 0.6 oct Cinematic, 1.1 oct Aggressive); applied per sub-block with multiplicative `SmoothedValue` (50 ms). The SVF recomputes coefficients on `setCutoffFrequency` - call per 32-sample sub-block only.
  - The class also exposes LP mode for the noise and delay/reverb send filters (shared implementation).

### StereoWidth
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::LinkwitzRileyFilter<float>` (LR4 low/high split at 150 Hz, `juce_dsp`) + custom mid/side matrix math.
- **Purpose:** Progressive stereo expansion that preserves the center and keeps low frequencies mono-compatible.
- **Parameters Affected:** tension, riseMode, lfoB (stereo movement)
- **Configuration:**
  - Split into low (<150 Hz) and high bands. **Lows: bypass the widener** (and as t increases, the low side channel is progressively collapsed: `S_low *= (1 - 0.8*smooth(0.3,1,t))`) -> mono-compatible sub energy.
  - **Highs:** `M' = M * midComp`, `S' = S * width` with `width = 1 -> 2.1` (Cinematic; Aggressive 2.4, Slow Burn 1.8), and `M' = M * midComp` where `midComp` is a mild power compensation (nominally `1/sqrt((1 + w^2)/2)`, clamped so Mid is never attenuated by more than 1.0 dB). Final constants are set empirically in the Phase 3 width tests.
  - **Movement:** lfoB adds +-`moveDepth` modulation to the width factor (slow sway) and a small Side-channel rotation (rotation by angle `a = moveDepth*lfoB*0.35 rad` in the M/S plane - preserves energy, avoids hard phase cancellation) rather than L/R delay (avoids comb filtering).
  - No inter-channel delays (Haas) anywhere - keeps mono-sum cancellation minimal. A mono-sum test (`L+R` energy vs `L,R` average energy at t=1) must stay within 3 dB.
  - Width smoothing 100 ms.

### ReverbEngine
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::Reverb` (Freeverb-derived; modern `prepare(ProcessSpec)` / `process(ProcessContext)` API - Critical Pattern #17) + `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, Linear>` for pre-delay (juce::dsp::Reverb has none) + `StateVariableTPTFilter` HPF/LPF on the send.
- **Purpose:** Atmospheric parallel reverb with tension-controlled wet level, decay, damping, pre-delay, and spatial depth, tails that ring out naturally.
- **Parameters Affected:** tension, riseMode (via mapping)
- **Configuration:**
  - **Send/return architecture (ported from DROP, lesson "wet mix hits 0 while internal buffers still hold decaying content"):** the module is always internally 100% wet (`wetLevel=1, dryLevel=0`). `sendGain` gates what enters the reverb; `returnGain` scales what is mixed back. The reverb instance is ALWAYS processed so the tail keeps evolving. Return gain uses **asymmetric smoothing** (150 ms attack / 700 ms release) so dropping tension lets tails ring out instead of being gated by the smoother.
  - `roomSize` 0.35 -> 0.92 (decay), `damping` 0.7 -> 0.30 (brighter/longer as tension rises; but a Phase-3 test pins RT60 rough scaling), `width` 0.6 -> 1.0 (spatial depth), pre-delay 0 -> 38 ms (Cinematic; Slow Burn up to 60 ms) via `DelayLine`, send HPF 120 -> 220 Hz (source definition: keeps low-end out of the tail), return LPF 14 kHz -> 7 kHz at max decay so the tail does not mask the source's top end. `freezeMode` never engaged.
  - `setParameters` is called once per sub-block with already-smoothed values (juce::dsp::Reverb also has a 10 ms internal smoother on damping/feedback).
  - Return level: `-inf` at t=0 (`smooth(0.08,0.55,t)` onset), up to -9 dB (Cinematic) relative to wet bus.
  - Reverb ducking against source is NOT implemented in v1 (avoid hidden dynamics); the HP/LP send/return filtering is the "source definition" mechanism.
  - **Fallback/upgrade path:** `ReverbEngine` hides the algorithm behind `prepare/setTargets/process` so a custom 8-line FDN (Hadamard feedback matrix, modulated delay lengths, per-line damping, RT60 control) can replace `juce::dsp::Reverb` without touching TensionEngine. Trigger: Freeverb metallic/ringing character judged unacceptable at 100% during Phase 3.x listening.

### DelayEngine
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, juce::dsp::DelayLineInterpolationTypes::Lagrange3rd>` x2 (`juce_dsp`) + `StateVariableTPTFilter` (feedback HP/LP) + custom tanh soft-clip in the loop.
- **Purpose:** Stereo tempo-synced ping-pong delay with filtered feedback and smooth delay-time transitions; never runs away.
- **Parameters Affected:** tension, sync, riseMode, lfoB (time wobble)
- **Configuration:**
  - **Time:** sync ON -> division picked by riseMode (Slow Burn dotted 1/4, Cinematic dotted 1/8, Aggressive 1/16 triplet... exact table in Algorithm Details), converted `ms = 60000/bpm * beats`; sync OFF -> fixed ms equivalents (Slow Burn 560 ms, Cinematic 375 ms, Aggressive 190 ms). Max 2.0 s: if tempo makes a division exceed 2 s, halve until it fits. Buffers allocated for 2.5 s at max sample rate (192 kHz) per channel.
  - **Tension does NOT switch divisions** (would cause pitch glides at discrete points); tension drives wet level, feedback and filter. The division only changes when riseMode/tempo changes, always through the time slew.
  - **Smooth time transitions:** target delay (in samples) passes through a one-pole slew (250 ms) before setting `DelayLine::setDelay` per sample -> tape-style glide instead of clicks; Lagrange3rd interpolation keeps modulation clean. Tiny lfoB modulation (+-0 -> 0.9 ms) adds chorus-like movement.
  - **Ping-pong:** input is summed to mono-ish send, fed to L line; L output feeds R line input and R output feeds L line (cross-feedback), so repeats alternate.
  - **Feedback:** 0 at t=0 -> 0.62 (Cinematic) / 0.55 (Slow Burn) / 0.72 (Aggressive) at t=1, `smooth(0.45,1,t)` onset (spec: feedback rises around 75%). HARD CAP 0.85 in code regardless of mapping. In-loop: HPF 180 Hz, LPF 9 kHz -> 3.2 kHz as feedback rises, then tanh soft clip (drive 1.0) so no loop can exceed ~+/-1 internally, and DC blocking via the HPF. Per-sample `std::isfinite` guard on the loop write; on failure the delay lines are reset (flag raised for OutputSafety counters).
  - Wet return level `smooth(0.2,0.7,t)`, up to -8 dB; asymmetric smoothing like the reverb (120 ms attack / 600 ms release) with same send/return split so repeats ring out when tension is pulled down.

### SaturationEngine
- **JUCE Class:** Custom - first-order ADAA (antiderivative anti-aliasing) tanh waveshaper (`F(x) = log(cosh(x))`), no `juce::dsp::Oversampling` (see Decisions).
- **Purpose:** Musical soft saturation that raises perceived intensity (harmonic energy) without heavy distortion.
- **Parameters Affected:** tension, riseMode
- **Configuration:**
  - `y = (F(drive*x_n) - F(drive*x_{n-1})) / (drive*(x_n - x_{n-1}))` / normalisation; for `|x_n - x_{n-1}| < 1e-5` fall back to `tanh(drive * 0.5*(x_n + x_{n-1}))`. Small asymmetric bias (+0.08, scaled by drive) adds even harmonics for "warmth"; a 12 Hz one-pole HPF removes the DC the bias creates (wet path only).
  - Drive 1.0 -> 4.2 (Cinematic; Aggressive 7.0; Slow Burn 3.0) with `smooth` + power curve; **level-compensated** (`makeup = 1/ (drive^0.5)` approx, tuned so RMS at -18 dBFS pink noise changes < 1.5 dB across the drive range) so intensity != volume jump.
  - **Parallel amount** `satAmount = smooth(0.15, 0.95, t)^1.3 * modeScale` blends processed against dry-in-chain (`out = x + amount * (sat(x) - x)`): keeps transient definition (spec: preserve source definition).
  - Per channel state (x1). Smoothing 50 ms on drive and amount. Zero latency.

### OutputSafety
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (no `juce::dsp::Limiter` - it hides a fixed 4:1 compressor stage at -10 dBFS, see factory memory `juce_limiter_hidden_compressor`).
- **Purpose:** Prevent NaN, infinities, runaway feedback and uncontrolled peaks - while being EXACT identity when the plugin is at rest.
- **Parameters Affected:** none directly (reads engagement `e`); output trim applied AFTER it (spec).
- **Configuration:**
  1. **Scrub:** per sample, non-finite -> 0 (bit test via `std::isfinite`); counts events into an atomic diagnostic counter; if > 0 in a block, signals TensionEngine to `reset()` feedback modules (delay lines, reverb, filters) at the next block boundary (no allocation; clears preallocated memory).
  2. **Soft ceiling:** C1-continuous knee: identity for `|x| <= 0.891` (-1 dBFS); above, `y = sign(x) * (k + (1-k) * tanh((|x|-k)/(1-k)))` with `k = 0.891` - asymptote exactly 1.0 (0 dBFS), no gain-pumping, no lookahead, no latency. Blended in by the safety-engagement `s = smooth(0.0, 0.03, t)`: `out = x + s*(safe(x) - x)`. At t=0, `s = 0`, so full-scale input (or >0 dBFS float) passes untouched.
  3. **Runaway guard:** a slow wet-bus peak tracker (attack 5 ms, release 200 ms); if wet bus peak > +9 dBFS for > 100 ms, the guard applies a feedback-gain clamp (multiplies delay feedback by 0.5 and reverb send by 0.5, smoothed) until it recovers. This catches pathological host states without a pumping limiter in normal use.
  4. **Output trim** `-24..+12 dB` (smoothed, 20 ms) after the safety stage.
  - Dynamic character is deliberately "clip-like knee, not a limiter": at max tension the engine's own gain staging (level compensation) keeps the signal below the knee for typical material; the knee catches only transients.

### Zero-Tension Transparency / Engagement (cross-cutting)
- **Purpose:** 0% = bit-transparent passthrough (spec + parameter-spec). Stateful filters/saturators cannot be bit-exact, so transparency is a *routing property*, not a property of the processors.
- **Design:**
  - `e = smooth(0, 0.02, t_smoothed)` (the *engagement*, 15 ms smoothed). 
  - Series chain (Pre-Filter -> Mod -> Saturation -> Stereo) produces `proc`. The wet bus is `wet = dry*(1-e) + proc*e + noise + delayReturn + reverbReturn`.
  - Final: `out = dry*(1-mix) + wet*mix`, then OutputSafety, then output trim.
  - At t=0: `e=0`, all gains are snapped to exactly 0.0 (SmoothedValue targets of 0 snapped when |v| < 1e-6), so `wet == dry` bit-exactly (`x*1.0f + 0.0f*...`; products with exact 0 and 1 are exact in IEEE float). With `mix` anything and output trim 0 dB, output == input bit-for-bit once settled and tails < -120 dB. 
  - Tail ring-out: when tension returns to 0 while reverb/delay still ring, returns are non-zero until the tail envelope trackers drop below -120 dBFS; only then is exact identity/fast-path restored (transparency criterion is "after tails decay").
  - Test: render 10 s of random float noise at t=0 for all three rise modes, sync on/off, block sizes {1,32,512,4096}, sample rates {44.1k..192k}: `memcmp(in,out)==0`.

## Processing Chain

```
                         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                         │ HostTransport (bpm, ppq, isPlaying) ──► LFOEngine A/B
                         │ APVTS: tension, mix, output, sync, riseMode  │
                         └──────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                                            ▼
                              TensionMapping(t, riseMode, modeBlend)
                                   │  TensionTargets (~30 values, evaluated per 32-sample sub-block,
                                   │  each destination smoothed with its OWN time constant)
                                   ▼
INPUT (mono→dup / stereo)
  │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────► dry (clean copy, never touched)
  ▼
Input Gain (tension-driven drive trim, level-compensated)         ← sat drive pre-gain
  ▼
Pre-Filter: HP (rising) + resonant BP sweep (parallel blend)      ← FilterEngine, lfoA cutoff mod
  ▼
Modulation: amplitude tremolo (lfoA)  /  stereo + delay mod taps (lfoB, applied in later stages)
  ▼
Saturation (ADAA tanh, parallel amount)                           ← SaturationEngine
  ▼
Stereo Processing (LR4 split 150 Hz; M/S width on highs; side rotation lfoB)  ← StereoWidth
  │  = proc
  ├───────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │               ▼                                               ▼
  │      Delay send (ping-pong, FB HP/LP + tanh, lfoB time wobble)   Reverb send (HPF, pre-delay → juce::dsp::Reverb → LPF)
  │               │ delayReturn (asym smoothing)                     │ reverbReturn (asym smoothing)
  │               └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
  │                                      │
NOISE (independent parallel generator) ──┤   NoiseGenerator: xorshift32 → pink/white blend → HP/BP/LP,
  gain/brightness/tremolo from mapping   │   amp from dB-linear curve (exactly 0 at t=0), lfoA tremolo
                                         ▼
 wet = dry·(1−e) + proc·e + noise + delayReturn + reverbReturn
                                         ▼
 mixed = dry·(1−mix) + wet·mix                                   ← MIX (independent dry/wet)
                                         ▼
 OutputSafety: scrub NaN/Inf → soft ceiling knee @ −1 dBFS (blended by s) → runaway guard
                                         ▼
 Output trim (−24..+12 dB)  ← OUTPUT
                                         ▼
OUTPUT  ──► Telemetry (lock-free): tension (smoothed), output peak, wet RMS → Visualizer (UI thread)
```

**Routing notes:**
- **Feedback loops:** only inside DelayEngine (cross-fed ping-pong) and the Freeverb comb/allpass network. Both are individually bounded (feedback cap, in-loop tanh, DC-blocking HPF, per-sample finite guard). The only inter-module "loop" would be a send from the post-stereo `proc` into delay and reverb (feed-forward). Delay → reverb is NOT chained in v1 (both are parallel sends) to keep feedback analysis simple.
- **Noise is a parallel ADD** to the wet bus (not a series insert). It is included in the wet bus so MIX scales it - at MIX 0% the plugin is dry-only. (Open question flagged: users may expect noise independent of MIX; spec §3 says "Maintain independent dry/wet routing" - interpreted as dry path is independent of the effect path; revisit in UI review.)
- **Send/return split** for delay and reverb: send gains follow the tension map; return gains use asymmetric (slow-release) smoothing so tails survive downward automation.
- Mono hosts: engine duplicates mono to stereo on entry, averages L/R on exit (width/ping-pong collapse gracefully; test mono-sum behavior).
- No sidechain, no MIDI.

---

## System Architecture

### File I/O System
Not applicable. No file I/O, no samples, no preset files on disk in v1 (spec lists a `Presets/` directory - treat as factory preset *state* documents applied via the APVTS in later phases; no runtime file reads on the audio thread).

### Multi-Output Routing
**Bus configuration:** one stereo input + one stereo output (default). Supported layouts: mono->mono, stereo->stereo (via `isBusesLayoutSupported`). No sidechain, no aux outputs.
- `BusesProperties` MUST be set in the AudioProcessor constructor (Critical Pattern #4):
  ```cpp
  BusesProperties()
      .withInput ("Input",  juce::AudioChannelSet::stereo(), true)
      .withOutput("Output", juce::AudioChannelSet::stereo(), true)
  ```
- `isBusesLayoutSupported`: require `getMainInputChannelSet() == getMainOutputChannelSet()` and set in {mono, stereo}.
- DAW compatibility: standard effect; nothing exotic.

### MIDI Routing
Not applicable. `NEEDS_MIDI_INPUT FALSE`, `IS_SYNTH FALSE`. Host tempo/transport only (below).

### Host Tempo / Transport (Feature 12)
- `juce::AudioPlayHead* ph = getPlayHead(); if (ph) if (auto pos = ph->getPosition()) { bpm = pos->getBpm(); ppq = pos->getPpqPosition(); playing = pos->getIsPlaying(); }` - JUCE 8 `getPosition()` returns `Optional<PositionInfo>`; the deprecated `getCurrentPosition()` must NOT be used (spec §2: avoid deprecated APIs).
- Read once per host block, copied into a POD `HostTransport` passed into the engine; tempo changes mid-block are not sample-accurate (acceptable: LFO/delay target slews absorb them).
- Fallback BPM 120 when unavailable; Standalone uses the fallback.
- DROP's `MusicalClock` may be reviewed for reuse, but TENSION needs only BPM and a one-shot transport-start phase alignment, so a ~40-line local helper is preferred over importing DROP's larger clock.

### State Persistence
**What state is saved:** APVTS parameters only (tension, mix, output, sync, riseMode). No UI state requiring persistence in v1 (window size fixed). Plugin identity for state: use a `ValueTree` type name `TENSION_STATE` and a `schemaVersion` property for future migration.

**Serialization format:** `apvts.copyState()` -> `XmlElement` -> `copyXmlToBinary` in `getStateInformation`; `getXmlFromBinary` + `replaceState` in `setStateInformation` (standard JUCE pattern); validate tag name; invalid data is ignored (defaults retained).

**JUCE classes:** `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState`, `juce::ValueTree`, `juce::XmlElement`, `juce::MemoryBlock`.

**Restore behavior:** deterministic - after `setStateInformation` all smoothers are `setCurrentAndTargetValue`'d at the next `prepareToPlay`/first block (no ramp from stale values on load), RNG seeds are constant (noise reproducible), no hidden state. Test: set params -> save -> new instance -> restore -> identical render.

### Visualizer Telemetry (Feature 14)
- Audio thread writes a small struct of `std::atomic<float>`: `tensionSmoothed`, `outPeak` (decaying max, per block), `wetRms`, `noiseLevel`, `lfoPhaseA` (for animation seeding). UI reads at 60 Hz with a `juce::Timer`. No locks, no queues, no allocation.
- The visualizer is a *reactive meter/animation* - NOT an FFT analyzer. All animation state (particles/ring rotation) lives in the UI and is independent of audio processing (spec §6).

## Parameter Mapping

| Parameter ID | Type | Range / Default | DSP Component | Usage |
|-------------|------|-----------------|---------------|-------|
| tension | Float | 0-1 (0-100%), default 0, linear skew | TensionMapping -> ALL modules | Master macro; each destination evaluated on its own nonlinear curve; also drives engagement `e` and safety blend `s` |
| mix | Float | 0-1 (0-100%), default 1.0 | TensionEngine final mix | `out = dry*(1-mix) + wet*mix`; 20 ms smoother; noise/reverb/delay returns are inside `wet` |
| output | Float | -24..+12 dB, default 0 dB (step 0.1) | Output trim after OutputSafety | `dbToGain`, 20 ms smoother |
| sync | Bool | default true | LFOEngine, DelayEngine, NoiseGenerator tremolo | ON: LFO rate = bpm-scaled cycles/beat, delay time = beat division; OFF: free Hz / fixed ms |
| riseMode | Choice | Slow Burn, Cinematic (default), Aggressive | TensionMapping | Selects curve profile (start/end/exponent per destination, LFO shape per destination, delay division, noise ceiling); crossfaded 600 ms on change |

Parameter IDs are stable (`juce::ParameterID{ id, 1 }`): `tension`, `mix`, `output`, `sync`, `riseMode`. Text conversion shows percent (0 decimals) and `dB` (1 decimal). Automation resolution: floats are fine; `riseMode` is a stepped `AudioParameterChoice`; `sync` an `AudioParameterBool`.

---

## Algorithm Details

### Master Tension Map (Cinematic profile reference; other modes in table below)

All destinations use the same input `t`, never feed one another, each uses its own curve. Notation: `S(a,b,t)` = smoothstep clamp, `E(t,k)` expo, `P(t,p)` power.

| Destination | Curve (Cinematic) | Start -> End | Onset (spec stage) |
|---|---|---|---|
| engagement `e` | S(0,0.02,t) | 0 -> 1 | 0% transparent; instantly engaged by ~2% |
| safety blend `s` | S(0,0.03,t) | 0 -> 1 | |
| Input drive trim / sat drive | P(S(0.15,0.95,t),1.4) | 1.0 -> 4.2 | harmonic intensity builds 25%+ |
| sat parallel amount | P(S(0.15,0.95,t),1.3) | 0 -> 0.85 | |
| HP cutoff | oct(20 Hz, 5.0 oct, E(t,2.4)) | 20 -> ~640 Hz | subtle at 10%, thinning 60%+ |
| BP sweep blend | S(0.2,0.9,t)*0.30 | 0 -> 0.30 | spectral movement 40%+ |
| BP center | oct(300 Hz, 4.9 oct, P(t,1.6)) | 300 Hz -> 9 kHz | |
| BP resonance Q | 0.9 -> 3.2 (capped 4) | | |
| LFO rate (free) | oct(0.15 Hz, 5.9 oct, E(t,2.0)) | 0.15 -> ~9 Hz | modulation speed 40% -> faster 75% |
| LFO rate (sync) | cyclesPerBeat 0.125 -> 4 (soft-snap ladder) | | |
| LFO amp depth | S(0.08,0.85,t)*0.35 | 0 -> 0.35 | "subtle movement" at 10% |
| LFO filter depth (oct) | S(0.1,0.9,t)*0.6 | | |
| LFO stereo/move depth | S(0.2,0.9,t)*0.5 | | |
| LFO delay-time depth | S(0.4,1,t)*0.9 ms | | |
| Noise level | gate S(0.04,0.28,t) * dB-lin(-66 -> -16, E(t,2.6)) | -inf -> -16 dBFS | "25% noise begins emerging" |
| Noise brightness (pink->white) | S(0.1,0.95,t) | 0 -> 1 | |
| Noise HPF | oct(80, 5.0 oct, E(t,2.0)) | 80 -> 2.5 kHz | |
| Noise BP/LPF top | oct(2500, 2.7 oct, P(t,1.4)) | 2.5 kHz -> 16 kHz | |
| Width factor | 1 + 1.1*S(0.25,0.95,t)^1.2 | 1 -> 2.1 | "wider at 60%" |
| Low side collapse | 0.8*S(0.3,1,t) | | |
| Reverb return | S(0.08,0.55,t) * -9 dB ceiling | -inf -> -9 dB | "atmospheric" 60% |
| Reverb roomSize | 0.35 + 0.57*S(0.1,0.9,t) | | |
| Reverb damping | 0.7 - 0.4*S(0.1,0.9,t) | | |
| Reverb pre-delay | 38 ms * S(0.3,1,t) | | |
| Reverb width | 0.6 + 0.4*S(0.2,0.9,t) | | |
| Delay return | S(0.2,0.7,t) * -8 dB ceiling | | atmospheric delay at 60% |
| Delay feedback | 0.62*S(0.45,1,t) (hard cap 0.85) | | feedback rises 75% |
| Delay FB LPF | oct(9 kHz, -1.5 oct, S(0.45,1,t)) | 9 -> 3.2 kHz | |

**Rise mode deltas** (each is a re-parameterisation of the above, not a gain change):

| Aspect | Slow Burn | Cinematic | Aggressive |
|---|---|---|---|
| Curve exponents (modulation/noise/sat onset) | late & gentle (onset +0.1, exponent x1.4) | baseline | early & steep (onset -0.05, exponent x0.7) |
| LFO max rate (free) | ~4 Hz | ~9 Hz | ~16 Hz |
| LFO depths | x0.7 | x1.0 | x1.5 |
| LFO shapes (amp / filter / stereo / delay) | sine / sine / triangle / sine | triangle / sine / sine / sine | rev-saw / S&H(filter, slewed) / triangle / sine |
| Noise ceiling | -20 dBFS | -16 | -12 |
| Noise color emphasis | pink, filtered | pink -> white | white + BP sweep |
| Sat drive max | 3.0 | 4.2 | 7.0 |
| Width max | 1.8 | 2.1 | 2.4 |
| Reverb: onset / size / ceiling | earlier (0.05), size 0.97, -7 dB | baseline | later, shorter (size 0.82), -11 dB |
| Delay division (sync) | dotted 1/4 | dotted 1/8 | 1/16 triplet |
| Delay feedback max | 0.55 | 0.62 | 0.72 |
| Delay free time | 560 ms | 375 ms | 190 ms |

These numbers are initial design values; Phase 3.5 tunes them by listening and metric tests (see Tests). Constraint: every curve is monotonic in t (tested), and modes must differ measurably (test: noise RMS @ 50%, LFO rate @ 75%, sat THD @ 100% differ by >= 2 dB / 25%).

### Smoothing Times (per destination, not universal)

| Destination | Smoothing |
|---|---|
| tension (raw, host automation) | 20 ms linear |
| engagement `e`, safety `s` | 15 ms |
| mix, output | 20 ms |
| noise gain | 40 ms; noise brightness/cutoffs 60 ms (log) |
| filter cutoffs / Q | 50-80 ms (multiplicative) |
| LFO rate | 120 ms (log domain); LFO depth 50 ms |
| saturation drive/amount | 50 ms |
| stereo width | 100 ms |
| reverb return | 150 ms attack / 700 ms release (asymmetric) |
| reverb size/damping | 250 ms (+ juce internal 10 ms) |
| delay return | 120 ms / 600 ms |
| delay feedback | 200 ms |
| delay time | 250 ms one-pole slew (tape glide) |
| riseMode crossfade | 600 ms |

Smoothers: `juce::SmoothedValue<float, ValueSmoothingTypes::Linear|Multiplicative>` stepped per 32-sample sub-block (`skip(n)` / `getNextValue()` per sub-block with interpolation for gains used per-sample).

### Per-feature algorithm notes (3.2.1 summary)
- **Tension -> risers psychoacoustics:** professional risers combine (a) rising high-passed noise (spectral energy upward), (b) accelerating amplitude/filter modulation (rhythmic urgency), (c) widening + reverb bloom (spatial expansion), (d) rising harmonic density (saturation), and (e) pitch/filter rise. TENSION omits pitch-shifting (avoided: DROP lesson #26, blind granular fails; spec doesn't request it).
- **Pink noise:** Kellett refined filter, ~ -3 dB/oct to within 0.05 dB 9.2 Hz-22 kHz; normalise by RMS after construction (constant).
- **ADAA tanh:** reduces aliasing of the saturation without oversampling latency; with drive <= 7 and wet-only parallel amount, residual aliasing is acceptable at 44.1 kHz; the test checks aliased-bin energy for a 5 kHz sine at drive max stays > 40 dB below fundamental.
- **LR4 split for width:** LinkwitzRileyFilter outputs sum to flat magnitude (allpass-complementary), so recombining low + high at width=1 is flat; verified in test (`|out/in|` within 0.05 dB with width 1).

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies
- TensionMapping -> every DSP module (sole source of destination targets).
- Host transport -> LFOEngine (rate, one-shot phase align) and DelayEngine (time).
- LFOEngine -> FilterEngine (cutoff), StereoWidth (rotation/width), DelayEngine (time wobble), amplitude tremolo (series chain + noise).
- FilterEngine (series) -> SaturationEngine -> StereoWidth: order matters (see below).
- StereoWidth output (`proc`) -> Delay send and Reverb send (spatial effects receive the widened signal).
- NoiseGenerator -> wet bus directly (no sends: noise itself is bright and wide; sending it to reverb is an option "noise-to-reverb" deliberately left OFF in v1 to avoid mud; revisit in tuning phase as a 0..0.3 send).
- Engagement `e` -> wet-bus dry/proc crossfade; safety blend `s` -> OutputSafety.
- OutputSafety scrub flag -> TensionEngine `reset()` of feedback modules.
- Engine telemetry -> Visualizer (UI thread, read-only).

### Parameter Interactions
- **tension x riseMode:** profile selection changes all curves; handled by 600 ms `TensionTargets` crossfade.
- **sync x tempo x riseMode:** delay division from mode, time from BPM; if resulting time > 2 s halve. If `sync` toggles, LFO rate switches between Hz and cycles/beat through the 120 ms log slew and delay time through the 250 ms slew - no clicks.
- **tension x mix:** mix scales the whole wet bus (including noise/returns). tension=100%, mix=0% = dry only.
- **tension (delay feedback) x reverb return:** both ramp in the 40-75% region; level compensation (return ceilings at -8/-9 dB) avoids cumulative loudness runaway; OutputSafety guard is the backstop.
- **output:** independent of everything; after OutputSafety by spec (so +12 dB trim can exceed 0 dBFS intentionally).
- **saturation drive x level:** compensated so drive changes loudness < 1.5 dB.

### Processing Order Requirements
1. **Capture dry** copy first - never altered (bit-exactness depends on it).
2. **Input gain / drive trim** - before saturation so it acts as drive; compensated after.
3. **Pre-Filter (HP + BP sweep)** BEFORE saturation: removes lows so saturation doesn't generate intermodulation mud from sub energy, and BP sweep feeds harmonic generation (spectral movement is distorted, gives "scream").
4. **Amplitude modulation** after filter, before saturation (so tremolo depth also modulates drive = dynamic intensity); applied as a smooth gain, never a hard gate.
5. **Saturation** before Stereo: stereo widening should work on the *final* harmonic content; also keeps nonlinear processing mono-coherent (no L/R decorrelation from independent nonlinear tails... states per channel are identical for identical signals).
6. **Stereo** before sends: delay/reverb inherit the width.
7. **Delay and reverb in parallel** (sends from `proc`).
8. **Noise** generated independently, added at the wet bus.
9. **Wet crossfade with engagement -> Mix -> OutputSafety -> Output trim.** Trim last per spec.
- Parallel: noise generator, delay, reverb all compute independently each sub-block.

### Thread Boundaries
- **Audio thread:** `processBlock` only. Reads APVTS floats via `getRawParameterValue()->load()` (atomic), reads play head, evaluates mapping, runs chain, writes telemetry atomics. No allocation, no locks, no I/O, no logging.
- **Message/UI thread:** parameter attachments, editor, visualizer timer (60 Hz) reading telemetry atomics, `prepareToPlay` (host-defined thread; allocation is allowed there).
- **Communication:** APVTS atomics (params) and `std::atomic<float>` telemetry (audio -> UI). No lock-free queue needed.

---

## Implementation Risks

### TensionMapping (curve design / musicality across 4-32 bars)
**Complexity:** MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** HIGH (musical, not technical)
**Risk factors:** "Sounds musical over 4/8/16/32 bars" is subjective; curves tuned at one speed can feel front- or back-loaded at another. Interaction of ten rising destinations can sum louder than expected.
**Alternative approaches:** (1) Per-destination curves exposed as data tables loaded from a constexpr struct so retuning is trivial; (2) A loudness-compensation stage (RMS follower on wet bus vs dry, correct slow) if cumulative gain >3 dB.
**Fallback architecture:** Add a slow (1 s) RMS-based wet-bus level compensator targeting <= +6 dB over input RMS at t=1; documented but initially OFF.
**Mitigation:** Offline render harness producing per-curve metric logs (noise RMS, centroid, width, RT60 estimate, loudness vs t) over a 0..1 ramp; assert monotonicity + max step; listening checks at 4/8/16/32-bar equivalents (linear ramp of t over those durations at 120 BPM); constexpr data tables.

### ReverbEngine (juce::dsp::Reverb quality at long decay)
**Complexity:** MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** MEDIUM
**Risk factors:** Freeverb's comb network can sound metallic; no built-in pre-delay; parameter changes during ring-out can produce level swells; tail masks source.
**Alternative approaches:** Custom 8-line FDN with Hadamard matrix and modulated delay lines (RT60-controlled per-line damping filters) - higher quality, ~150 lines; Reuse DROP's ReverbModule send/return wrapper (already tested).
**Fallback architecture:** Primary = `juce::dsp::Reverb` + predelay + send/return filtering (low risk, proven in DROP). Fallback/upgrade = FDN behind the same `ReverbEngine` interface if a Phase 3.x listening test rejects the Freeverb character.
**Mitigation:** Isolation behind interface; HP send / LP return to retain definition; asymmetric return smoothing; RT60/tail tests (tail decays < -60 dB within expected time; no NaN after parameter sweeps).

### DelayEngine (stability and glides)
**Complexity:** MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** MEDIUM
**Risk factors:** Runaway feedback with ping-pong; time slew causes pitch glide that may sound off when tempo jumps; tempo-sync + 192 kHz buffer size; interpolation click on large jumps.
**Alternative approaches:** Cross-fade two delay taps on time change (no glide, more CPU); fixed-time (no sync glide).
**Fallback architecture:** If glide objectionable -> dual-tap crossfade (equal-power, 120 ms) instead of continuous slew.
**Mitigation:** Hard feedback cap 0.85 + in-loop tanh + HP/LP + finite guard; 100-run randomized stability test at max settings for 60 s render; time-jump test checks no sample discontinuity > threshold.

### SaturationEngine (aliasing without oversampling)
**Complexity:** LOW-MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** LOW
**Risk factors:** ADAA numeric ill-conditioning for tiny deltas; level compensation tuning; DC from bias.
**Alternative approaches:** `juce::dsp::Oversampling<float>` 2x polyphase IIR (adds latency; breaks dry/wet alignment and zero-tension bit-exactness unless dry is delay-compensated); `juce::dsp::WaveShaper` with tanh (aliases at high drive).
**Fallback architecture:** `Oversampling` 2x linear-phase FIR with a matching dry delay line (latency reported via `setLatencySamples`) - only if alias test fails.
**Mitigation:** fallback branch for |dx|<1e-5; DC HPF; alias-bin test.

### StereoWidth (mono compatibility and phase)
**Complexity:** MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** MEDIUM
**Risk factors:** M/S width above 2x can cancel in mono; LR4 crossover phase vs. dry path (the crossover sits only in the wet/proc path; since `proc` is crossfaded with dry by `e`, a phase offset could cause comb when e is mid - mitigated because `e` reaches 1 at t=0.02).
**Alternative approaches:** Simple M/S gain without crossover (cheaper; low-end side energy not protected); frequency-dependent width via allpass decorrelation.
**Fallback architecture:** Remove crossover, use M/S with HPF on the Side channel at 150 Hz (a one-pole HP on S) - no phase split of mid.
**Mitigation:** Mono-sum energy test (<= 3 dB loss at t=1), correlation measurement, flat-sum test of LR4 recombination.

### NoiseGenerator
**Complexity:** LOW  **Risk Level:** LOW
**Risk factors:** Excess noise masking source; pink-filter constants; determinism across platforms (float ops identical; RNG integer ops are).
**Alternative approaches:** Pre-baked noise tables (memory, loop artefacts); `juce::Random` (global state, not reproducible with host threading).
**Fallback architecture:** None needed.
**Mitigation:** Seeded xorshift32; golden-hash test (first 4096 samples hash), RMS rise test, silence-in/noise-out test; ceiling levels conservative.

### LFOEngine host sync
**Complexity:** MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** MEDIUM
**Risk factors:** Continuous rate vs musical grid; ppq alignment; tempo automation.
**Alternative approaches:** Discrete rate ladder with crossfaded dual LFOs.
**Fallback architecture:** Pure continuous tempo-scaled rate (no snap, no ppq alignment).
**Mitigation:** Phase accumulator (never ppq-locked per sample); log-domain rate slew; unit tests for shape ranges, wrap, S&H determinism.

### OutputSafety
**Complexity:** LOW  **Risk Level:** LOW
**Risk factors:** Bit-transparency vs protection tension; false-positive guard triggers.
**Alternative approaches:** Always-on soft clip (not transparent), `juce::dsp::Limiter` (hidden 4:1 compressor - rejected), `juce::dsp::Compressor` as brickwall (needs lookahead).
**Fallback architecture:** Hard clamp at +/-4.0 plus scrub (no knee) if knee interacts badly.
**Mitigation:** Blend `s` tied to tension; identity unit test; NaN injection tests.

### Overall Project Risk
**Overall complexity:** HIGH (by module count and coordination; each module individually LOW-MEDIUM).
**Highest risk component:** TensionMapping tuning (musicality). ~40% of risk; code risk is low, creative risk is high.
**Recommended approach:**
1. Foundation + parameter shell and transparent passthrough with engagement routing (proves bit-exactness early).
2. Core series modules (Filter, Sat, Width, LFO) with tests.
3. Sends (Delay, Reverb) and Noise.
4. TensionMapping + three modes + tuning harness.
5. Safety hardening, then GUI (native).

---

## Architecture Decisions

### GUI Technology: Native JUCE (RECOMMENDED) vs WebView
**Decision:** Build the GUI with **native JUCE graphics** (`juce::Component` + custom `LookAndFeel_V4` subclass + a `TensionKnob` and a `Visualizer` Component), NOT WebView. **Flagged for the user's confirmation** because the factory default is WebView.

| Criterion | Native JUCE | WebView (factory default) |
|---|---|---|
| Spec §6 compliance | Exactly as written ("native JUCE graphics and custom LookAndFeel") | Deviation from authoritative spec |
| Visual needs | 1 oversized knob + circular visualizer + 4 small controls: trivially drawable with `juce::Graphics` (gradients, arcs, glow via layered strokes) | HTML/CSS/canvas/SVG easily supports it too |
| Reactive visualizer | `juce::Timer`/`VBlankAttachment` at 60 Hz reading atomics - no bridge | JS requestAnimationFrame + C++->JS event bridge (Pattern #20) |
| Reliability / ops | No NEEDS_WEB_BROWSER, no WebView2 runtime on Windows (see factory CI lessons), no ES-module/relay gotchas (#7, #8, #12, #13, #15, #16, #21, #23, #24), no cached-page issues | All of those patterns apply |
| Automation gestures | `juce::Slider` + `SliderParameterAttachment` brackets gestures natively | Must bracket manually in JS (#23) |
| Design iteration speed | Slower to iterate on visuals (recompile) | Fast browser iteration of mockups |
| CPU/memory | Lighter; no browser process | Heavier |
| Factory pipeline | Requires skipping the HTML mockup step; gui-agent writes C++ components from a native design brief | Standard pipeline |

**Rationale:** The UI is minimal and the spec explicitly asks for native graphics; the heavy WebView pitfalls (and Windows WebView2 runtime dependency) buy nothing for a single knob. The visualizer can be made premium with `Graphics` (radial gradient glow, rotating arc segments, noise-driven jitter) and `ColourGradient`.
**Alternatives considered:** WebView (above) - reconsider only if the user wants browser-quality effects (blur/bloom shaders) that are costly natively; hybrid is rejected (complexity).
**Tradeoffs accepted:** Fewer visual effects; no HTML mockup artifact (Stage 3 gui-agent should produce a short native design spec instead of `v1-ui.html`).
**Pipeline impact:** CMake: `juce_gui_basics`, `juce_graphics`, no `juce_gui_extra` web browser, `NEEDS_WEB_BROWSER FALSE`, no BinaryData UI resources required (fonts embedded optionally). Parameter attachments: `SliderParameterAttachment`, `ButtonParameterAttachment`, `ComboBoxParameterAttachment`.
**When to revisit:** user vetoes native; or visual requirements exceed `Graphics`.

### Zero-tension transparency by routing, not by processor purity
**Decision:** `wet = dry*(1-e) + proc*e + additive sources`, with exact-zero snapping, plus an at-rest fast path.
**Rationale:** Filters/saturators can't be bit-exact; routing-level gating can.
**Alternatives:** Bypass-crossfade at mix level (then MIX semantic muddy); per-module true-bypass (6 places to get right).
**Tradeoffs:** `dry` is held separate (small extra memory copy).

### ADAA saturation instead of oversampling
**Decision:** First-order ADAA tanh, zero latency.
**Rationale:** Latency would break dry/wet alignment and bit-exact transparency; ADAA gives most alias suppression for soft curves.
**Alternatives:** 2x/4x `juce::dsp::Oversampling` (latency, CPU); plain `WaveShaper` (aliasing).
**Revisit:** if alias test fails at drive 7 (Aggressive).

### juce::dsp::Reverb first, FDN as upgrade
**Decision:** Reuse the DROP-proven pattern (juce::dsp::Reverb, send/return, 100% internal wet) + pre-delay and filtered send/return.
**Rationale:** Lowest risk, fastest to a working signal chain; abstraction allows upgrade.
**Alternatives:** Custom FDN immediately (more code, more tuning), convolution (needs IRs).

### Custom OutputSafety (no juce::dsp::Limiter)
**Decision:** scrub + C1 soft knee at -1 dBFS blended by tension + runaway guard.
**Rationale:** `juce::dsp::Limiter` embeds a 4:1 compressor at -10 dBFS (factory finding) - not transparent. A true lookahead limiter would add latency.

### Delay division fixed by rise mode, not by tension
**Decision:** Avoid tension-driven discrete division changes.
**Rationale:** Discrete jumps cause pitch glides at specific tension points; keeps automation smooth. LFO acceleration conveys urgency instead.

### Control-rate sub-blocks of 32 samples
**Decision:** Parameter/mapping updates every <=32 samples.
**Rationale:** Avoids zipper noise (smoothers advance in small steps) while keeping filter coefficient recalculation cost bounded; block-size invariance test.

### Noise inside the wet bus (MIX scales it)
**Decision/Open question:** noise subject to MIX. If the user prefers noise independent of MIX (generate riser from silence with MIX at 0), expose later as a request. Documented in Routing notes.

### Mono/stereo only (no surround)
**Decision:** mono->mono, stereo->stereo. Spec §2 says mono/stereo.

---

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety
- All parameter reads via atomic `getRawParameterValue()->load()`; DSP modules own all state; no shared mutable state between channels except the engine-level struct updated in the audio thread.
- Telemetry via relaxed atomics. `prepareToPlay`/`releaseResources` allocate/free; `processBlock` never allocates (verify with a debug allocation-guard test).

### Performance
Estimated at 48 kHz stereo (single core, rough): Reverb ~4-6%, Delay ~1-2%, Filters (SVF x ~6/ch incl. noise, send filters) ~2%, Saturation ADAA (log/cosh per sample) ~1-3% (use `std::log(std::cosh)` approximation with fast path for |x|>~9: `|x| - ln2`), Width ~0.5%, Noise ~1%, LFO + mapping ~0.2% (once per 32 samples). Total target < 15% of one core at 48 kHz, < 40% at 192 kHz. Hot paths: ADAA log/cosh, Lagrange3rd delay reads.

### Denormal Protection
- `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` at top of `processBlock`.
- Feedback paths: add/subtract 1e-18 offset trick avoided; instead flush `|x|<1e-20` to 0 in delay feedback write and filter states are inherently protected by FTZ/DAZ.
- At-rest fast path avoids running tail math at all.

### Sample Rate Handling
- 44.1-192 kHz. All time constants specified in seconds/ms, converted in `prepare`; filter coefficients computed from live `sampleRate`; delay buffers sized by `maxDelaySeconds * sampleRate` (2.5 s). Cutoffs clamped to 0.45 fs. Reverb/ pre-delay sized for 80 ms max. Re-`prepare` on any rate/block change; `reset()` clears state.
- `juce::dsp::Reverb` is fixed-structure Freeverb tuned at 44.1k (its comb lengths scale by sample rate internally in JUCE 8 `Reverb`'s `prepare`).

### Latency
- Zero algorithmic latency (no lookahead, no oversampling, no FFT). `getLatencySamples() == 0`. Pre-delay is musical wet-path delay, not reported.

### Tails
- `getTailLengthSeconds()`: report conservative 8 s (reverb at max room + delay feedback ring-out) so hosts keep processing after clips end (risers need to ring out). Alternatively dynamic; v1 returns 8.0.

### Numerical stability checks
- NaN/Inf injection into input, extreme parameter jumps (0 -> 1 -> 0 each sample-block), 60 s soak at max settings in all modes, denormal soak (silence after loud) - all required to produce finite output with peak <= 1.0 + trim.

## Research References

### Professional Plugins
1. **Dada Life Endless Smile** - the one-knob "Intensity" build plugin that popularised the category; single macro drives multiple effects (filter, noise, reverb); validates the one-knob-to-many mapping concept.
2. **Rys Up Audio RysUpSweep** - one-knob "Intensity" insert riser with 7 modes, level-match and "club safe" options; confirms mode-based remapping and level compensation as expected features.
3. **BOOM Library LiftFX** - synthesizes risers from scratch (not processing); validates noise-from-silence generation as a distinct, wanted capability.
4. **UJAM Finisher / Baby Audio Transit 2** - macro-driven transition effects with multiple effect modes; confirms audience expectation for coordinated multi-FX macros.
5. **Ableton "Easy Riser" free rack** - auto filter + delay + reverb + EQ behind one macro: the minimal precedent for what TENSION generalises with nonlinear per-destination curves, noise, stereo and safety.
(Vendor pages were used; they are self-promotional and give no DSP internals. Algorithmic choices come from general riser sound-design practice plus the DROP implementation.)

### JUCE Documentation (JUCE 8; mapped from memory of the module structure and the factory's DROP/KICKR code; Context7 MCP was not available in this session - verify exact signatures during Stage 1)
- `juce::dsp::StateVariableTPTFilter<float>` (juce_dsp): LP/BP/HP, `setCutoffFrequency`, `setResonance`, `setType`, `prepare/process/processSample`.
- `juce::dsp::LinkwitzRileyFilter<float>` (juce_dsp): `setType(lowpass/highpass/allpass)`, `processSample(channel, x, outLow, outHigh)`.
- `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, Lagrange3rd>` (juce_dsp): `setMaximumDelayInSamples`, `pushSample`, `popSample(ch, delay, updateReadPointer)` - Critical Pattern #25: readPos advances once per sample.
- `juce::dsp::Reverb` (juce_dsp): `Parameters{roomSize, damping, wetLevel, dryLevel, width, freezeMode}`, `prepare(spec)`, `process(ctx)` - Pattern #17.
- `juce::SmoothedValue<float, Multiplicative/Linear>` (juce_audio_basics).
- `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState`, `AudioParameterFloat/Bool/Choice`, `ParameterID{id, version}`, `SliderParameterAttachment`/`ComboBoxParameterAttachment`/`ButtonParameterAttachment`.
- `juce::AudioPlayHead::getPosition()` -> `Optional<PositionInfo>` (`getBpm`, `getPpqPosition`, `getIsPlaying`).
- `juce::ScopedNoDenormals`.
- NOT used: `juce::dsp::Limiter` (hidden compressor), `juce::dsp::Oversampling` (latency), `juce::Random` (non-deterministic across hosts), `juce::dsp::FFT` (none needed).

### Technical Resources
- DROP source (`plugins/DROP/Source/DSP/NoiseModule.*`, `ReverbModule.*`, `DelayModule.*`, `WidthModule.*`, `SaturationModule.*`, `FilterModule.*`, `MusicalClock.*`) - port send/return pattern, noise seeding approach, dB-linear curves.
- Parker/Esqueda/Bilbao, "Reducing the Aliasing of Nonlinear Waveshaping Using Continuous-Time Convolution" (DAFx-16) - first-order ADAA.
- Paul Kellett pink-noise filter; Linkwitz-Riley crossover; Dattorro/Jot FDN literature for the reverb upgrade path.
- Freeverb (Jezar) - behaviour of juce::dsp::Reverb.

## Notes

- **Open questions for the user (flagged):** (1) Native JUCE GUI vs factory-default WebView - recommendation: native (spec §6). (2) Should noise be subject to MIX (current design) or independent? (3) Mono->stereo layout (mono in, stereo out) not supported in v1.
- **Spec vs factory note:** spec §8 lists `Tests/` and `Presets/`; the factory console-test harness (RunTests.cpp style used by KICKR/PRISM) satisfies "DSP tests pass". Presets are optional post-1.0.
- **Required test list (Phase 3-6):** zero-tension bit-exactness (all modes/block sizes/rates); silent-input noise emergence (RMS monotone in t; ~-inf at t=0); NaN/Inf injection; 60 s max-feedback soak per mode; automation zipper test (max |second difference| of output while t ramps over 1/4/16 s); sample-rate matrix {44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, 176.4, 192}; block size matrix {1, 7, 32, 64, 512, 4096}; mono vs stereo; mode metric differences; state round-trip; deterministic noise golden hash; LFO shape/sync tests; mono-sum energy; reverb tail decay; denormal soak.
- DROP 1.0.0 remains untouched; TENSION is a new plugin with its own plugin code and product name.
